result.planSummary: Implemented Story 5 (message edit and cascade): a new shared cascade module (src/domains/messages/internal/cascade.ts) derives the clear-set structurally from the message → turn → chunk walk over existing derived_form rows, supersede-deletes still-queued old-version items (reported on the result), and enqueues replacements at each group's max source version + 1 inside the mutation's transaction. messages.edit validates through the deleted-filtered read (turn_open / message_not_found refusals), applies content + blocks + token re-stamp via new store.ts helpers (readMutableMessage / applyMessageEdit mirroring projectEvent's counted fields), runs the cascade, and returns the MutationResult — one synchronous commit, with enqueue pokes riding onCommit so background mode rebuilds with no further call. The source-version check (existing single write path in work-queue complete()) is provoked by TC-5.4's delayed-double recipe: a real claimed pre-edit item held across the edit completes after the post-edit replacement is queued and discards as stale_discarded. CLI: new src/cli/messages-mutate.ts and `lhc messages edit --message/--message-id --content` wiring with parity proven through the spawned binary.

findingsFixed: Atomicity fault injection initially targeted a queued conflicting row, which the cascade's supersede step would have deleted before the enqueue; switched to a claimed row so the replacement insert genuinely collides mid-cascade and forces the rollback path

Cascade source-version bump computed per rebuild group as max(existing versions) + 1 rather than per-form +1, so the two turn forms (one shared turn_derivation item) can never enqueue at diverged versions
findingsSurfaced: TC-5.4 timing: the edit must land inside the delayed double's 400ms provider window after the poll observes the handler start; edit completes in single-digit milliseconds so the margin is wide, but an extremely loaded CI machine could in principle let the v1 completion land first and fail the mid-flight coexistence assertion

messages.listMessages and turns reads do not yet filter deleted_at (Story 6 scope); TC-5.5's deleted-target leg stamps deleted_at below the SDK and only asserts the edit refusal reads through the filtered validation view

specDeviations: TC-5.6's CLI parity legs live in a new test/cli-process-mutations.test.ts instead of test/cli-process-work.test.ts named by the story's test mapping: that file is hash-locked by the Story 1 red manifest (green may add files, not edit) — same precedent Story 4 set with cli-process-report-repair.test.ts

TC-5.4 holds the claimed pre-edit item via an unawaited manual-mode work.drain promise rather than background mode + drainSettled, so the drain report's stale_discarded disposition is directly assertable (the test plan's storage-contract note requires that assertion); the claimed-item-held-across-the-edit overlap is identical, and background mode is separately proven by the edit-and-walk-away test
CLI accepts both --message (the story's and tech design's spelling) and --message-id (the house convention used by report/requeue); both parse into the same input

For tool_call blocks the edit's content string lands verbatim as the new arguments value (estimate re-stamped from its serialization, mirroring projection); the design's edit signature is content: string for all kinds and only text-kind edits are TC-covered — noted for the Story 6/verifier record
